title: Fix crashes on generators, suppliers, lazy sequences and short FreeSASA radii
body:
#### Reference Issue

Found while typing the nanobind wrappers' arguments for #9601. This PR also contains what was #9610 (FreeSASA radii).

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.

Several wrappers convert the elements of a Python iterable or sequence to raw pointers and use them after the element's last reference is gone. A generator drops each element as it advances, and a supplier builds a new molecule each time it is indexed, so the pointers dangle, and the call segfaults, aborts, or raises something like `ValueError: vector`. What each wrapper set did before this change, where "lazy" is a supplier or any sequence that builds its items when indexed:

| function | nanobind | Boost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TanimotoSimilarityNeighbors` and the other neighbor functions | crashed on a generator or lazy sequence | crashed on a lazy sequence; `TypeError` for a generator |
| `BulkTanimotoSimilarity` and the other bit vector bulk functions | worked | crashed on a lazy sequence; `TypeError` for a generator |
| the sparse int vector bulk functions | worked | `ArgumentError` for anything but a list |
| `FingerprintGenerator.GetFingerprints` and the other three | crashed on a generator or lazy sequence | crashed on a lazy sequence; `TypeError` for a generator |
| `GetFPs`, `GetCountFPs`, `GetSparseFPs`, `GetSparseCountFPs` | crashed on a generator or lazy sequence | `ArgumentError` for anything but a list |
| `GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen` | read freed memory for a generator | ignores `patterns`, even a list |
| `MolDraw2D.DrawMolecules`, `MolsToJSON` | crashed on a generator | read freed memory for a generator |
| `RGroupDecomposition(cores)` | crashed on a generator | worked |
| `EnumerateLibrary` | crashed once the caller dropped its reagent list; crashed on a `None` reagent | crashed on a `None` reagent |
| `FindMCS` | crashed on a supplier | worked |
| `RunReactants` | crashed on a lazy sequence | `ArgumentError` for anything but a tuple or list |
| `MaxMinPicker`/`LeaderPicker.LazyBitVectorPick` | crashed on a lazy sequence | crashed on a lazy sequence |
| `AllowedAtomsValidation`, `DisallowedAtomsValidation` | worked | read freed memory for a generator |

After this change neither wrapper set crashes or reads freed memory on these inputs, and the Boost similarity and fingerprint functions and `RunReactants` accept what the nanobind ones do: any iterable, or any sequence for `RunReactants`, which indexes its argument. Reading freed memory shows up as a crash, a wrong result, or an error such as `RuntimeError: vector`, depending on what reuses it. `GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen` ignoring `patterns` under Boost is unchanged and tracked in #9601.

The fixes:

- Iterated arguments are collected into a list of references that outlives the pointers. Nothing is copied: the elements stay alive until the call returns, which is what passing a list already costs, and a generator's elements are held the same way. In the Boost wrappers the same list lets these functions take any iterable, not only a list or a sized sequence.
- The lazy pickers hold each element they index.
- `RGroupDecomposition`, `EnumerateLibrary`, `FindMCS` and `RunReactants` take shared ownership through the `boost::shared_ptr` caster in `RDBoost/boost_shared_ptr.h`, as the Boost wrappers do, instead of wrapping each molecule in a no-op deleter. For `EnumerateLibrary` that deleter kept the pointers after the call returned; the library now keeps its reagents alive while it exists, as the Boost wrapper does.
- `EnumerateLibrary` raises `ValueError` for a `None` reagent, as `RunReactants` does.
- `SmilesMolSupplier::length()` reads to the end of the stream to count lines and left the supplier marked as finished, so `list()` on a fresh supplier, which calls `__iter__` and then `__len__`, returned nothing in both wrapper sets. It now clears the stream and restores that state, as `SDMolSupplier` does. The fingerprint functions above iterate through the same path, so a `SmilesMolSupplier` passed to them hit this too.

**FreeSASA radii.** `FreeSASA::calcSASA` handed `&radii[0]` and `mol.getNumAtoms()` to FreeSASA without checking `radii.size()`, so a `radii` vector shorter than the molecule was read past its end, and an empty one dereferenced an empty vector. From Python, with the 1d3z test protein, in both wrapper sets:

| `radii` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one per atom | 5004.8 | 5004.8 |
| one extra entry | 5004.8 | `RuntimeError` |
| first 10 | `nan` | `RuntimeError` |
| first 1 | 0.0 | `RuntimeError` |
| empty | segmentation fault | `RuntimeError` |

`calcSASA` now requires exactly one entry per atom and fails a precondition otherwise; a longer vector is rejected too, instead of having its extra entries silently ignored. `test_basics` in `testFreeSASA.py` also compared `(sasa - expected) < 1e-5` without `abs()`, so any result below the expected area passed; it now uses `abs()`, and the computed areas match the expected values to within 1e-7.

**DCLV radii.** `DoubleCubicLatticeVolume` indexes `radii` by atom index without checking its length, the same way, so two radii for a thirteen-atom molecule gave a surface area of 158 where the van der Waals radii give 259 — a plausible number read from beyond the end of the vector. An empty vector still asks for the van der Waals radii, as leaving the argument out does; any other length fails a precondition.

#### Any other comments?

The tests are in the shared test files and run under both wrapper sets. Each compares the result for a generator, supplier or lazy sequence against the same call with a list, and `testNoneReagent` checks the `ValueError`. They pass with this change, and every input they use crashed, read freed memory, or raised the errors in the table under at least one wrapper set without it. The Boost `AllowedAtomsValidation` read-after-free only showed up with `PYTHONMALLOC=malloc MallocScribble=1`, so it has no test. `v2_suppliers_catch.cpp` gains a section for `SmilesMolSupplier::length()`, which fails without the fix and passes with it. `testMolSupplier`, `fileParsersCatchTest`, `fileParsersIteratorsTest`, `testMultithreadedMolSupplier` and `multithreadedSupplierCatchTest` also pass. `test_radii_length` passes radii that are too short, empty, and one entry too long; without the check the run crashes under both wrapper sets, and with it `testFreeSASA.py` and the C++ `testFreeSASALib` pass. `testDCLVRadiiLength` and a section in `Code/GraphMol/Descriptors/catch_tests.cpp` do the same for `DoubleCubicLatticeVolume`, including that an empty vector matches the default; with the check removed only those assertions fail, and `descriptorsTestCatch` and `testMolDescriptors.py` pass with it.

Built locally with each wrapper set. These pass: `testBV.py`, `testSparseIntVect.py`, `testGenerators.py`, `testMolInterchange.py`, `test_rgroups.py`, `testFMCS.py`, `testReactionWrapper.py`, `testPickers.py`, `testMolStandardize.py`, the supplier tests in both `rough_test.py` files, `testMolDraw2D.py` (nanobind), and the new `testEnumerations.py` tests. Some local failures happen with or without this change because the build mixes two C++ runtimes (see #9601): four serialization tests in `testEnumerations.py` abort, and under Boost any `MolDraw2DSVG` aborts when destroyed. With the drawer kept alive, the new drawing test's check passes under Boost.

`ReleaseNotes.md` records both `radii` requirements under backwards incompatible changes.
